plan: My value is $25. In a single-round auction with independent values, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders likely have values near $25 too. I'll bid strategically at $24.5 - just below my value - to potentially win if others bid similarly, minimizing overpayment while still having a good chance of winning.

My value is $18. In a first-round sealed bid auction, rational strategy suggests bidding close to, but below my true value. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders might bid strategically around their own values. I'll aim to win by bidding slightly above my value to account for potential competitor strategies, but not so high that I risk negative profit. A bid around $16-$19 seems optimal.

My value is $31. In a first-price sealed bid auction, I want to bid strategically. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$49, rational bidders will likely bid below their true value. I'll aim to bid close to my value but slightly under, perhaps around $28-$29, to maximize potential profit. This allows some buffer against overpaying while still having a good chance of winning. The key is balancing winning probability with minimizing potential overpayment.
